item.title: ATEEZ’s San Personally Addresses Viral Dating Rumor With Mystery Woman
item.description: ATEEZ's San addressed viral dating rumors, stating they are untrue and expressing discomfort with being tracked by fans.
item.content:encoded:
Days after a video showing ATEEZ’s San out with a woman went viral, the star has personally addressed the dating rumors surrounding him.
Earlier this week, while San was in Italy for a Milan Fashion Week appearance with Dolce & Gabbana, a fan-taken video made waves across social media. In the clip, San was seen walking with a woman, leading some to believe his secret “relationship” had been exposed.
Now, San has broken his silence on the fan-artist communication platform Fromm. The idol admitted he is “taken aback” by how people keep tracking him down, adding that anything beyond a chance meeting is “a little uncomfortable.”
But I don’t know how they find out.Every time I go, people follow me…I’m taken aback.Running into people by chance is totally fine, but if it’s not that, it’s a little uncomfortable LMAO.
— San
San went on to reveal that he hasn’t wanted to bring it up at all because he thought fans might worry, but added that ATEEZ’s agency, KQ Entertainment, had contacted him too.
I didn’t want to mention it because I thought you all might worry. First of all, the company contacted me too, but it’s not [true]. So don’t worry, and enjoy a delicious meal LMAO.
I guess I need to explain what I’m talking about. There’s a dating rumor going around, but it’s not true
— San
Turning to fans who film such videos, San didn’t hold back. “Secretly taking photos is wrong,” he wrote, urging, “Let’s not commit crimes, before you get caught.”
Secretly taking photos is wrong too. Let’s not commit crimes, before you get caught. And I’m okay, but the people who are connected to me would have a really hard time, so that shouldn’t happen.
— San
Likewise, fans across social media have slammed those who followed San and took videos of him, rejecting their claims that they ran into him by chance.
Alongside San’s own messages, KQ Entertainment also addressed the rumors and revealed the identity of the woman in question.

item.title: Dexter Lawrence is adding, among many things, personality to the Bengals defense
item.description: The article highlights how Dexter Lawrence brings personality and a unique dynamic to the Bengals' defense.
item.content:encoded:
Zac Taylor is in a unique position. He's the head coach of the Bengals and their offensive play-caller.
In his position, Taylor, like a CEO, is also in charge of managing this team's personalities. Most of those personalities have been on offense in Taylor's tenure.
Now, the defense has some. Not only is the Bengals' defense revived. It has personality, especially up front and with Dexter Lawrence.
Lawrence is the tone-setter of the Bengals' defense. That comes in the form of on-field production, but it also comes with having a little fun on the field trash-talking.
"He just loves it. I think he's contributed to the personality of our defense," Taylor said after Friday's practice. "Not only are they talented and confident, and playing with this really good chemistry, but they've got a really big personality as a whole, and he's obviously a big part of this, and that's what's fun."
Lawrence was mic'd up during the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Houston Texans in Week 2. It was incredible to listen to, with Lawrence demonstrating elite trash-talking abilities.
It's something we haven't really seen from a Bengals' defense in quite some time. The S.W.A.T. Team had personality back in the 80s, but Bengals' defenses since really haven't it… until now.
"With the mic'd up stuff, everybody gets to see kind of what we see from him, (defensive tackle) Jonathan Allen, and everybody kind of combining together," Taylor said. "And it probably gets a couple of the other guys out of their shell a little bit."
Don't be surprised if you see other mic'd-up segments and soundbites from the Bengals or NFL Films showcasing Lawrence and the Bengals' defensive line trash-talking their opponents. The Bengals' defensive line is getting a lot of attention. They have talented players, but they also have players with personalities.

item.title: Liverpool make fresh plans to finally sign long-term target
item.description: Liverpool is reportedly planning a renewed attempt to sign defender Micky van de Ven from Tottenham Hotspur.
item.content:encoded:
Over the summer, Liverpool were linked with a whole host of players.
Arne Slot was sacked and Andoni Iraola was brought in which meant that plenty of change was already scheduled to take place.
And, while things have started off quite slowly with only a few wins, the fact that the Reds are still unbeaten across all competitions is fairly impressive.
Indeed, Liverpool did manage to bring in a fair few new faces over the summer but, it still feels like more additions and potentially even exits are needed.
That is, especially if Iraola wants to get his first-team squad back to their best.
So, the fact that new links with players are continuing to emerge despite the transfer window being shut is rather reassuring with a previously-linked player now making his way back onto the Reds' shortlist.
Liverpool want to sign Micky van de Ven from Tottenham again
One of the main areas of Liverpool's team that needed upgrading in the summer was their defence.
Ibrahima Konate and Andy Robertson both exited Anfield and, while the Scotsman was replaced by Kostas Tsimikas, the Reds still needed a new centre-back which is where Jeremy Jacquet came in.
However, even after both of these moves, thanks to injuries and unavailability, Liverpool were still short at the back which resulted in Ronald Araujo joining on a season-long loan.
And, to the surprise of many, the Uruguayan has been pivotal to the Reds this term.
But, before Araujo and Jacquet were signed, many other players emerged as potential options with Micky van de Ven being one of them.
Unfortunately, that deal never came to fruition and the Dutchman ended up signing a contract extension with Tottenham but, since Spurs have failed to meet expectations once again, it seems like Liverpool are about to try and make a move for the Dutchman once again.
"Liverpool are plotting a move to sign Tottenham Hotspur star Micky van de Ven as they put plans in place to strengthen at the back," Football Insider wrote.
"Andoni Iraola's side are making long-term plans to sign a new centre-back as they prepare for Virgil van Dijk to leave the club upon the expiry of his contract next summer.
"The centre-back's fellow countryman has been high on their list for a long time, and following Tottenham's slow start to the new season, they could try to take advantage.
"Roberto De Zerbi's side are understood to be reluctant to lose their captain, and will demand a significant fee, especially if they are to sell to a Premier League rival.
"Van de Ven, however, is believed to be open to a move to Anfield given Tottenham's recent struggles and would welcome the opportunity to discuss terms over a move."
Liverpool signing Micky van de Ven would be a bold move
On paper, Van de Ven looks like he'd be a perfect signing for Liverpool.
However, since he's only just signed a new deal with Spurs and hasn't really been in the best run of form lately, it doesn't feel as good as what it did last season.
Since the Dutchman has extended his contract, it's very likely that he'd cost a hefty chunk of change for Liverpool to bring in.
But, with his lightning-quick speed, his versatility and experience, it is probably going to be hard to find another player who ticks all of those boxes.
That is, especially since left-back is a major problem area for Liverpool at the moment.
Obviously, many changes are expected to take place at Anfield over the next few months so the rumour mill is very likely to go into overdrive.
However, as long as Iraola and Julian Ward both know who they want to sign and for how much, that's all that fans can really ask for.

item.title: Gyokeres scores for Sweden, still looks miserable
item.description: Viktor Gyokeres scored for Sweden but appeared unhappy, reflecting his struggle for minutes and form at Arsenal this season.
item.content:encoded:
Viktor Gyokeres got the minutes and the goal he needed for Sweden against Romania, but his reaction suggested there is still more to come from the Arsenal forward.
Viktor Gyokeres scored the winner for Sweden against Romania on Friday evening, but the Arsenal forward still looked far from pleased.
With Kai Havertz fit this season, at least until his hamstring went while playing for Germany during the current international break, Gyokeres has found minutes and form hard to come by domestically.
He has played only 29 out of a possible 450 Premier League minutes and has totalled just 207 minutes across all competitions.
Given the stop-start nature of his involvement, it is perhaps unsurprising that he has yet to register a goal or assist for Arsenal this season and has generally looked frustrated when he has been on the pitch.
Unlike for most other Arsenal players, the international break, therefore, was seen as a good thing for Gyokeres.
It is a chance for him to get minutes and find some sharpness.
On Friday he did just that.
Even though he found the back of the net in the 43rd minute to win the game 2-1 for his country, he still looked fairly miserable as he did his trademark celebration.
He finished the match as Player of the Match with the highest rating of any player on the pitch, 7.9.
Across 76 minutes, Gyokeres completed 15 of 16 passes, created another chance and scored with the only opportunity that came his way, although the media in Sweden described his performance as 'edgy' at times and criticised his finishing after a second half miss.

item.title: Lazio Stalwart Reaches Verbal Agreement With Balotelli’s UAE Club
item.description: Lazio defender Patric is reportedly close to a move to UAE club Al-Ittifaq, which would help Lazio's financial standing.
item.content:encoded:
Lazio and Patric could be about to end their 11-year collaboration, with the defender closing in on a move to Al-Ittifaq.
The 33-year-old is a Barcelona youth product who made the move to the Italian capital club in 2015. The centre-back went on to make 244 appearances for the Biancocelesti, but his tally would have been larger if it wasn't for his recurring injury problems.
In fact, Gennaro Gattuso wasn't able to rely on the veteran in pre-season, which prompted the decision to drop him from his Serie A squad list alongside Luca Pellegrini. The club left two spots vacant, and one was later filled by Diogo Leite's late arrival.
Lazio Aiming to Offload Patric in the Coming Days
According to Il Messaggero, Lazio are keen to sell Patric before September 30, when they'll be expected to present their financial statement for the second half of the year. These figures will serve as the basis to determine whether the club will be allowed to operate on the market in January, as the risk of a transfer ban (or another net-zero market) persists.
Lazio Looking to Ditch Patric's Salary
Patric's age and expiring contract (June 2027) mean he's unlikely to generate a relevant transfer fee. But as the Roman newspaper explains, the defender's sale would allow the Aquile to save €3.5 million in gross salary.
Patric Could Join Mario Balotelli at Al-Ittifaq
While Il Messaggero only mentions that the player has received an offer from a Dubai-based club, Il Corriere dello Sport identifies Patric's suitor as Al-Ittifaq, an ambitious side that plays in UAE's second division. The club is currently coached by former Juventus defender Paolo Montero, and its ranks include former Serie A stars, Mario Balotelli and Douglas Costa.
Patric Agrees Terms With Al-Ittifaq?
CdS believes the Spanish defender already has an agreement in principle with Al-Ittifaq, who will try to conclude the operation before the Emirati transfer market closes on Monday. Therefore, the parties will try to finalise the deal in the next 48 hours or so.

item.title: Why Juventus could hand Man United their ultimate January transfer nightmare
item.description: Juventus' reported interest in Tyrick Mitchell could complicate Manchester United's plans for a January left-back signing.
item.content:encoded:
A left-back signing has been at the top of the agenda at Old Trafford.
Ideally, that transfer should have happened in the summer.
Despite Luke Shaw's ever-presence last season, it was clear he could not start every game, especially given how jam-packed the Red Devils' fixtures were this season.
Need for another top left-back at Manchester United
Getting another quality left-back to share the workload with Shaw made sense.
Unfortunately, however, a deal for such a player did not go through, after a move for top target Lewis Hall failed to materialise.
While that transfer was to be revisited next year, a move for Hall is no longer on the table. He has since committed his future to Newcastle, publicly highlighting his desire to stay there long term.
As a result, INEOS have had to turn to other targets, and one appealing option is Tyrick Mitchell.
Mitchell is in the final year of his contract at Selhurst Park, and given his quality and Premier League experience, he appeals to the 20-time English champions. They want him, and the player will reportedly find it hard to refuse.
Juventus keen on Tyrick Mitchell
Yet, as hope builds over this transfer, some less pleasing news is emerging from Italy.
Tutto Sport are reporting that, beyond David Raum, who has also been linked with a switch to M16, Juventus also want Mitchell.
They see him as the perfect option to bolster their left-back options. However, while they could also look to sign Mitchell when he becomes a free agent at the end of the season, they know it will be hard to compete with United, or any other top English side, in that race.
As a result, they are keen to move fast and convince Palace to let them sign Mitchell in January.

item.title: Little League reflections reveal need to 'keep sports about kids'
item.description: An author reflects on his Little League coaching experience, advising parents to prioritize sportsmanship and enjoyment over winning.
item.content:encoded:
Joining Little League was a natural fit for my family. Some of my fondest childhood memories are from being on a baseball diamond with my dad in the dugout. I lived for that experience. So, when I had two sons of my own, getting back to Little League just felt natural.
My coaching experience started with my older son, but I eventually spent time as either a manager or assistant coach for both of my boys in Little League, basketball, and flag football. The decade I spent coaching my sons and watching them move up through the levels of play taught me so much. At the same time, I was building my career as a sportswriter. The shared moments on the diamond with my sons and the lessons I learned from the players and families I worked with each season ultimately led to my weekly sports parenting column, "Ask Coach Steve," with USA TODAY.
What began as an opportunity to share a game I loved with my sons became an experience that shaped not only my career, but who I was as a father. My favorite moments from my sons' Little League years had little to do with the wins and losses I experienced as a coach. Instead, I remember drives home filled with conversations about sportsmanship as they both wrestled with what they could have done differently to prevent a tough loss.
I remember helping them work through disappointment and adversity. My one son was never selected to an All-Star team during his Little League years, but he persevered, and he is now playing at the collegiate level. Teaching them patience and rewarding them for good sportsmanship far outweigh the final score being in your favor at the end of a game.
For parents watching from the stands, my advice is to keep it fun and let them compete. I think back to the times where I would say too much to the hitter who was up to bat instead of letting them figure the situation out for themselves. Those are the moments that we don't realize could be life lessons if we just let them experience it. Letting a kid work through a challenge or a failure can help them better understand the purpose and benefits of the sport they are playing.
We can help guide them through that process from afar. One day, they will look back and realize the lesson they learned in that moment has been carried with them into their adult years. So, let your kids compete. Let them make decisions. Let them work through those difficult moments. Let them fail. Sit back, watch and enjoy the chance to see your kids play.
For the parents who step onto the diamond as a coach, my advice is two-fold. First, as a parent, be open with your kids and allow them to express themselves about what they need from you as both a parent and as a coach. If you just go to the field and yell at them and tell them what they are doing wrong – even if they have success – it will still be a frustrating experience that could lead them to quit.
My second piece of advice is to have an open mind with every kid on the team. It's not just your experience or your kid's experience. It's about every child on that team. Give every player your attention. Give every player opportunity to prove themselves, because even a small moment of success can go a long way to give them the confidence they need to come back next season. Little League is meant to be an inclusive environment where everyone can get something out of it, whether they are the star on the team or someone trying it out for the first time, and it takes the coaches to help create that environment.
After years of coaching, raising two sons, writing about youth sports and talking with families, I always come back to one idea – keep youth sports about the kids. That is a perspective that is lost in today's youth sports climate as parents push their kids to specialize in a sport and apply a ton of pressure to be great.
Last year, I interviewed two-time MLB All-Star Todd Frazier, who competed in the Little League Baseball World Series back in 1998, and he said, "no one's getting scouted at 12-years-old." At the Little League level, our job is to give kids the opportunity to play, learn, experience failure and success and just enjoy being a kid.
Those are the experiences my sons and I were lucky enough to share through Little League, and they are the experience I hope families continue to find on baseball diamonds for generations to come.

item.title: Jayden Maiava is ready to lead USC into battle against Oregon

On Saturday, USC will host Oregon in a West Coast clash at the Coliseum. Leading the Trojans into battle for the massive game will be redshirt senior quarterback Jayden Maiava.
A recent USC Athletics feature profiled Maiava and his journey from a humble childhood in Hawaii to USC's starting quarterback.

"At USC, being the quarterback means more than running the offense. It is a brand in its own rite that carries a unique responsibility and heritage. Through his personal growth, Maiava has defined what that role means to him and established his own place within it."
On Thursday, head coach Lincoln Riley said of Maiava, "He's the guy I want taking us into this game for sure." Against Oregon, USC's quarterback will have the opportunity to deliver his signature moment in Cardinal and Gold to date.

item.title: Tennessee Titans vs. New York Giants: Behind Enemy Lines
item.description: This article previews the Week 3 NFL game between the Tennessee Titans and the New York Giants, including insights on player performance and game strategy.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans will face the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, in Week 3. It will mark the Titans' first road game of the season and also give them another opportunity to get one in the win column.
Both the Titans and the Giants are in similar situations in 2026. Well, they were before the Giants lost Jaxson Dart for the season. Both teams have entirely new coaching staffs, and both teams have lots of new faces in the locker room. Both teams were optimistic about 2026 before it started, and now both teams are desperately trying to keep that hope alive.
Ahead of this competitive matchup, Titans Wire sat down with Dan Benton of Giants Wire to gain some insight into the next opponent.
Jameis Winston struggled against the Rams last week. What can we expect to see from him in his first start of 2026?
Benton: I think you'll see Jameis Winston being Jameis Winston with a greater emphasis on not turning the ball over, which is a non-negotiable with John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy. What I wouldn't do -- as so many have -- is overreact to how Winston looked on Monday night. He was thrust into a game unexpectedly early on and had to operate a game plan that had been designed for Jaxson Dart. That came on the heels of a summer in which he took no first-team reps with the other starters, so it wasn't exactly a recipe for success. With a full week under his belt and a game plan designed around his skill set, Winston should look more the part on Sunday afternoon, weather permitting.
Which skill player do you expect to step up this week? What specifically can we expect from this player?
This is going to be a Cam Skattebo game. Nagy already lamented his lack of use in Week 2, and given the early forecast, this game will be decided in the trenches and on the ground. I would expect a heavy dose of Skatt with Ricard leading the way up the middle, and then around the edges. He is sneaky fast and can get going laterally, which is something Najee Harris can't do. Skatt is also sure-handed and a good option out of the backfield, which will play to Winston's strength, with the downfield game likely impacted by rain and wind.
Brian Callahan and Dennard Robinson were both in Tennessee last year. What has their impact been like, and how will their presence affect the game this week?
Callahan seems like he's in an ideal role and made a lot of progress with Dart this offseason. It's a shame we can't see that play out over a full season. Wilson is always a defensive coordinator I've been impressed with, and that hasn't changed over two weeks, despite an ugly outing against Los Angeles. But it's hard to blame him considering he lost his father just days earlier. And while he says there are "no excuses," I think we can all recognize that his mind was likely elsewhere. He works well with the talent he has and builds game plans specific to players' strengths. However, he will be tested this week in the absence of Brian Burns, Paulson Adebo, and other key players banged up.
What's your biggest matchup concern against the Titans?
Jeffery Simmons vs. John Michael Schmitz. Easy. JMS has not developed the way the Giants have hoped, and he hasn't given the team a return on investment. He was dominated by Aaron Donald a week ago, and Simmons has the ability to take over games against inferior players. The Giants will have to scheme around that weakness or risk being dominated at the line of scrimmage in a game that will be decided there.
Who wins, and what's the final score?
Given the early weather forecast, this game has a chance to be ugly. Heavy rains and gusty winds will make throwing the ball difficult, and kickoffs and field goals even more difficult. That's actually good news for the Giants, who will be able to ride running back Cam Skattebo until the wheels come off. So long as they can prevent Jeffery Simmons from wrecking the game, Jameis Winston & Co. will come out with a 16-7 win.

Chambliss' mom and father, Trent, travel to every game Chambliss plays.

Chambliss is from Grand Rapids, Michigan

Chambliss is 24. He was born Aug. 24, 2002.
Trinidad Chambliss NIL deal
Chambliss is set to earn about $6 million this season, per the Wall Street Journal.

Chambliss has positioned himself to be an early-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. CBS Sports reported that scouts view him from anywhere as a second or third round pick to a player worthy of being picked early in the first round.

item.title: September is Emergency Preparedness Month: Lessons from the July 6 Tornado
item.description: An article discusses lessons learned from a July 6, 2026 tornado in Becker County, Minnesota, emphasizing emergency preparedness.
item.content:encoded:
The July 6, 2026, EF2 tornado just north of Detroit Lakes was a powerful reminder of how quickly severe weather can change a community. The tornado traveled more than six miles, with a path approximately 800 yards wide, affecting 94 homes and one business. Two minor injuries were reported, and thankfully, there were no deaths. The response and recovery efforts demonstrated the strength of our community while also reinforcing several important preparedness lessons. This information comes courtesy of Adam R. Douglas with Becker County Emergency Management and Vanessa Collmann with Becker County Public Health.
Know how you will receive alerts
Don't rely on just one source of information. Becker County residents can sign up for the CodeRED emergency notification system to receive time-sensitive emergency and general notifications by phone, text, and email.
Becker County also offers CodeRED Weather Warning notifications for severe weather. Visit co.becker.mn.us/codered to register and make sure your contact information is up to date.
Know where to take shelter
Identify the safest location in your home before severe weather strikes and make sure everyone knows where to go. A Tornado Watch means conditions are favorable for tornadoes — be prepared. A Tornado Warning means a tornado has been detected or indicated — take shelter immediately.
Keep an emergency go-bag ready
If your home is damaged or you need to evacuate, you may not have time to gather everything you need. Keep essential items together, including medications, identification, important documents, chargers, a flashlight and batteries, hygiene items and a change of clothing.
Prepare for power outages and other disruptions
Plan to be self-sufficient for at least three days. Have water, nonperishable food, flashlights, batteries and charging options available. Consider the needs of household members who rely on electricity for medical equipment or other essential services, and have a backup plan for extended outages.
Make a plan for your family, pets and business
Talk with your household about where you will shelter, how you will communicate and where you will meet if you become separated. Include pets in your emergency plans and know where they can safely go if you must evacuate. Businesses should also have plans for employee communication, evacuation and continuing essential operations during an emergency.
Know your neighbors
After severe weather, check on neighbors who may need additional assistance, including older adults, people with mobility or hearing challenges, or residents who may not live at the property year-round. Knowing your neighbors before an emergency can make it easier to look out for one another when help is needed.
The July tornado reminded us that preparedness needs to happen before the warning. When individuals, families and businesses are prepared, our entire community is better able to respond and recover when an emergency occurs.
September is Emergency Preparedness Month — a great time to make a plan, prepare an emergency go-bag, talk with your family, and know how you will receive emergency information.
For more information on preparing your family, business, pets and more, visit Ready.gov.

item.title: Sixers 3 goals: LeBron James just needs to be himself in Philly
item.description: This article outlines three goals for LeBron James's hypothetical upcoming season with the Philadelphia 76ers.
item.content:encoded:
In this new series, Sixers Wire looks at the 16 players, per Spotrac, that comprise the Philadelphia 76ers roster — 14 under standard contracts and the two players on two-way deals — and gives each three goals for the 2026-27 season.
The new season begins on Oct. 20, and training camp is right around the corner. Now is the time to begin previewing the new season of adventure that is Sixers basketball.
Up next in this series is megastar LeBron James. The future Hall of Famer joins the Sixers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers and he continues to be one of the best in the game after averaging 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, and 6.1 rebounds in the 2025-26 season. He will now look to make an impact in Philadelphia.
For James, his three goals are as follows:
Set that championship example
For James and the Sixers, the goal is obvious: get to the mountaintop in the NBA. James has been there four times in the past, as he won two titles with the Miami Heat, a title with the Cleveland Cavaliers, and one with the Lakers. While the Sixers were already one of the more talented teams in the league heading into the new season, they don't have those championship habits that James has developed over his career. It will be on James to be the one that sets the tone every single day and shows his teammates the arduous journey of what it takes to win a championship in the NBA. The lessons and examples he can pass down every day will be important for this group to build on.
Be a playmaker
James has one of the highest IQs a player can have in this game. He has been able to throw teams on his back just by making subtle eye or head movements in an effort to point his teammates in a certain direction to get them open looks within the offensive ecosystem. When considering the offensive talent that will be placed around him in Philadelphia, one has to believe James won't need to be that ruthless scorer as he has had to be in the past. Now, he can settle into more of a playmaking role and make sure Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, and Tyrese Maxey get their touches and looks while out on the floor.
Get after it defensively
Yes, James turns 42 in December. While he has been kicking Father Time's behind in every other aspect, it seems his age is affecting him a bit on the defensive end of the floor as of late. One has to believe that a lesser offensive burden in Philadelphia could make his life a bit easier and allow him to be more focused and active on the defensive end. If the Sixers can get James to even make a few plays in the passing lanes and allow Philadelphia to get out and run, then it will make life that much easier for everybody else within the system. It would allow the Sixers to get into their sets much quicker and allow them to find a rhythm.

item.title: 11 Highly Anticipated Books Everyone Will Be Reading this Fall
item.description: This article lists 11 highly anticipated books scheduled for release in the fall, featuring new works from popular authors.
item.content:encoded:
Readers, mark your calendars. September and October are some of the biggest months of the year for book releases, and this fall’s lineup does not disappoint. This publishing season sees the return of some of your favorite authors, back with much anticipated sequels or exciting new standalones.
As you settle into cozy season and start looking at your TBR, these are the brand new reads from your favorite blockbuster authors, all publishing this fall.
1
Partita by Barbara Kingsolver
This is Barbara Kingsolver’s first release since Demon Copperhead won the 2023 Pulitzer Prize.
Livia has made peace with her marriage and her modest life—that is, until she gets a phone call from an old lover, asking to meet up. As she decides whether or not to see him again, she relives her days as a poor music student in college, caught in a destructive love affair and filled with both ambition for her music and a sense that she does not belong.
2
Taipei Story by R.F. Kuang
R.F. Kuang (Yellowface, Katabasis) departs from the dark academia she’s known for with this coming-of-age novel. Chinese American college freshman Lily is spending the summer in Taipei, hoping to connect with her heritage. But as she struggles to click with her classmates and her family doesn’t want to answer her questions about their history, she finds herself feeling like a foreigner rather than feeling at home.
3
Hollywood, Ending by John Green
This book is John Green’s first return to fiction in nearly a decade, and it’s his first-ever novel for adults. In this book, the YA author turned nonfiction writer (The Fault in Our Stars, Everything Is Tuberculosis) turns his sights to the celebrity media machine. When actors Kai and Juniper get their big break being cast in a buzzy biopic about Andy Warhol, they find themselves both falling in love and struggling with their newfound fame.
4
Exit Party by Emily St. John Mandel
The Station Eleven and Sea of Tranquility author returns with another high-concept speculative fiction book.
In 2031, after the collapse of the United States, Ari attends an apartment party—but something is wrong. First, there are mysterious doppelgängers, and then the host disappears without a trace. This dizzying read explores two different futures—a surveillance state and a post-civil war U.S.—showing one life shaped by changing circumstances in very different worlds.
5
American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee
A hagwon is a private after-school academy common in Korea. This sweeping family drama by the author of Pachinko follows the once middle-class Koh family as their lives are upended by financial instability, moving between Seoul, Sydney, and SoCal to provide for their children’s futures.
With a large, rotating cast of characters and a long path through the Korean diaspora, this is an immersive epic about family, education, immigration, and duty.
6
Hollow Bones by Jodi Picoult
This book can be read as a standalone, but it does feature an adult version of a character from Picoult’s 2004 book My Sister’s Keeper.
When Molly was only two months old, her mother died in 9/11. Haunted by disasters, Molly runs a department for emergency preparedness and is married to a police polygraph expert. But when the unexpected happens, her life and her marriage are upended as she questions everything she thought she knew.
7
Big Little Truths by Liane Moriarty
This is the grown-up sequel to the hit Big Little Lies, which is also a TV series. The kindergarteners from the original book are now high schoolers, with all the attendant drama. Parents Madeline, Celeste, Jane, Renata, and Bonnie must deal with the challenges of middle age—and of a stranger asking dangerous questions that could unearth the secrets they’ve kept from their children.
8
The Witches of Cambridge by Alice Hoffman
Alice Hoffman just released a new book, timed to the release of the new film adaptation of her Practical Magic series.
In 1950s Cambridge, Ava and Lauren are both young women at Radcliffe College. They are inducted into the Lilith society, a secret organization of witches that dates back to colonial times. But as the shadow of McCarthyism takes over campus and girls go missing, Ava and Lauren realize the witch trials of history may not be over.
9
Peck & Peck by Bonnie Garmus
In the latest release from Bonnie Garmus (Lessons in Chemistry), Batter is a poetry-obsessed recent college graduate in NYC in the 1980s. When he gets a job at the esteemed poetry quarterly Peck & Peck, he finds his hands full with warring editors-in-chief, quirky poetry editors, and an obsession with finding the best writing and destroying the rest.
10
The Pirate Queen by Ariel Lawhon
This historical fiction from the author of The Frozen River is inspired by Grace O’Malley, the legendary Irish folk heroine. Grace was born to be a sea captain, but as a woman, she is expected to marry for an alliance and have children instead. But when she is betrayed by her husband and English incursions into Ireland become increasingly threatening, Grace must lead her people and fight to defend her land.
11

item.title: Best Superhero TV Shows of the Last Decade Ranked
item.description: This article ranks superhero TV shows from the last decade, highlighting their evolution towards realism and complex themes.
item.content:encoded:
From Wonder Man to Watchmen, these superhero TV shows of the last 10 years have redefined the genre with realism and cerebral themes. Here are the top picks ranked.
The superhero genre has seen a lot of traction over the past decade. From monster hits that revive comic book lore to animated series that dive into deeper themes, the options for superhero fans to choose from have been rich and varied. As audiences become more discerning, superhero shows have changed with the Zeitgeist, moving away from wacky antics and spandex pantsuits to ground themselves in realism and explore more cerebral topics like multiverses and alternate dimensions.
## Evolution of Superhero TV Shows
As with any popular theme that is in high demand, there are series that rose to excellence and those that did not. The following titles not only created terrific TV shows that anyone could enjoy, but did credit to their comic book heritage as well. Whether you are an aficionado of classic TV shows or are brand new to the fandom, there is something for everyone to enjoy. These are the most perfect superhero shows of the last 10 years, ranked.
## Top Ranked Superhero Series
10 Wonder Man (2026): It is tough to be an actor, and it is not easy to conceal that you have superhuman abilities either. The titular protagonist in Wonder Man has to deal with both. Simon Williams (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) goes on auditions and tries to hone his craft as a performer, all the while trying to keep his emotions in check, because if he lets loose, he can unleash a truly devastating power. At this pivotal time in his life, he is befriended by Trevor Slattery (Ben Kingsley), who has ulterior motives for getting close to him.
Wonder Man is a winner for comic fans and for those who love the entertainment industry. Although the amount of focus given to the entertainment industry seems self-serving, Wonder Man navigates both spheres and resonates on all the levels that it is meant to. Wonder Man sadly joins a growing list of shows that were beloved by audiences, but unceremoniously canceled by networks. The writing, and now it seems the series own fate, is revealing a deeper truth about the current state of the industry that feels foreboding.
9 Superman & Lois (2021-2024): In an intriguing shift on several Superman TV shows, Superman & Lois does not focus on the Man of Steel's upbringing, but on that of his children. In the much-beloved series, Clark Kent (Tyler Hoechlin) and Lois Lane (Elizabeth Tulloch) are married with two sons. As the two boys grow up, they learn about their father's abilities and must make decisions about their own fates and responsibilities.
Superman & Lois is the best Superman TV show ever done. It is an exciting look into the next chapter of the well-known figure's life and provides some powerful storylines about what marriage and parenthood would be like for someone who is extraordinary. Superman & Lois is a family drama at heart, and that foundation gives it a super-strength that other shows on this list do not possess. If you have not checked out this absolute winner yet, this is your sign.
8 Moon Knight (2022): A comic book TV series that blends elements of fantasy into the mix is Marvel's Moon Knight. Oscar Isaac stars as Steven Grant, a shy and introverted museum employee who undergoes a radical transformation. When he is able to summon the powers of an Egyptian moon deity named Khonshu (Karim El Hakim and F. Murray Abraham), he is tasked with undertaking some harrowing quests, and his regular, humdrum life begins to feel like a distant memory.
Moon Knight excels at introducing fascinating heroes and villains. The cast is exceptional, and Ethan Hawke is hypnotic as the manipulative and underhanded Arthur Harrow. There are dramatic plot twists in Moon Knight, and the special effects are on par with Marvel TV's level of excellence. Moon Knight is all the more impressive because it achieved success on its own as a standalone project. It did not get the bolster of a mention in the larger MCU, but audiences loved it anyway, proving that a great story is a great story, whether it has been hyped or not.
7 Watchmen (2019): Damon Lindelof's TV adaptation of the Watchmen comics is something greater than the sum of its parts. While it is not a faithful retelling of the comic series, it uses the essence of the story to hold a mirror up to modern society. Vigilantism is, at its core, a profound crusade for justice in the eyes of the perpetrator. Watchmen does not shy away from complex topics and attempts to boil down themes occurring and recurring throughout history into the essence of what it means to have law and order.
Watchmen is a dissection of the fight for virtue. It touches on the dichotomy that what is fair and right can be very different depending on who you ask. Since the series was so different from the comics, it was subject to some backlash and harsh review bombing. However, this did not deter the many viewers who have come to appreciate Watchmen for what it is, instead of what it is not. As the passionate response to the series proves, opinions and beliefs run deep within the human race, and Watchmen hit a nerve.

item.title: Buddy Sequel: Producer Tyler Davidson Wants Horror Unicorn Follow-Up
item.description: Producer Tyler Davidson expressed interest in making a sequel to the horror film "Buddy" with a $100 million budget.
item.content:encoded:
Producer Tyler Davidson says he wants to make a Buddy sequel, revealing he would revisit Casper Kelly's horror film with a $100 million budget.
Producer Tyler Davidson wants to make a sequel to Buddy, the horror film directed by Casper Kelly that turns cheerful 1990s children's television into something far more unsettling. In a recent interview, when asked which of his movies he would revisit with a budget of $100 million, Davidson named Buddy without hesitation, saying the answer would very easily be a sequel because there is so much more he wants to explore.
No second movie has been officially announced, but the producer behind the film is clearly not ready to leave the orange unicorn behind. The original movie, which features an enormous orange unicorn mascot who promises to be friends with everyone, follows a world in which children begin disappearing and the people around them become increasingly difficult to trust.
Buddy is described as funny, deeply strange, and far more interested in unsettling its audience than in delivering a familiar slasher experience. Casper Kelly, known as the creator of Too Many Cooks, uses the language of 1990s kids' television and pushes it into territory it was never meant to reach.
Within the film, the smiling host of Buddy's show hides far more than he wants viewers to know. That gap between a friendly surface and a threatening reality is part of what has drawn audiences to the movie and left many of them wanting another dive into Buddy's world.
The movie draws on the look and feel of a children's program that viewers might have watched every morning before school, provided their parents never checked what was actually on television. Its mascot promises friendship to everyone, even as children disappear and trust erodes in the world around them.
Casper Kelly's background in surreal, genre-bending comedy shapes Buddy's approach. Too Many Cooks became a viral sensation by stretching a familiar television format into something increasingly dark and disorienting, and Buddy applies a similar strategy to the conventions of kids' programming.
That stylistic choice means the film is less interested in jump scares or a standard slasher structure than in messing with the viewer's head. The result is a movie that is both funny and deeply strange, according to the description of its tone.
Audiences who left the film wanting more of Buddy's world share that impulse with one of the people who made it. Davidson's eagerness to return suggests the creative team sees unexplored material in the concept, though nothing has been confirmed beyond his stated interest.
Davidson did not offer specific plot details for a potential second film. He simply said there is much more he wants to explore, leaving open what a sequel might cover or how it would continue the story of the mascot and the children in his orbit.
A $100 million budget scenario is hypothetical for now, raised as part of the interview question rather than as a confirmed plan. Even so, the producer's immediate answer shows where his interest lies among his own body of work.
For fans of the first movie, the key fact remains that no sequel has been announced. Any follow-up would depend on further development, and Davidson's comments represent enthusiasm rather than a green light.
The original Buddy stands as a film that mixes the vocabulary of children's television with horror elements, anchored by a mascot whose friendly promise contrasts with the danger around him. Whether that world returns to the screen is still an open question.

item.title: Explosive plays spark Thurston's 12th straight win over Springfield
item.description: Thurston High School's football team secured their 12th consecutive victory over rival Springfield with a 47-22 home win.
item.content:encoded:
There are plenty of emotions that arise after a big rivalry win.
For Thurston coach Justin Starck, in the moments following his team's 12th consecutive win over crosstown foe Springfield, the immediate feeling was relief.
"I don't know what it is, but I know when you lose, you're miserable. You're absolutely miserable when you lose this one," Starck said. "It's not a good feeling. For our seniors, we don't want them to have to live with that. Every year, just get another one."
For yet another year, Starck and the Colts won't have to worry about any of that.
Thurston rolled to a 47-22 home win over crosstown rival Springfield on Sept. 25, adding another dominant entry to their ever-growing winning streak. With the win, the Class 5A No. 8 Colts improved to 3-1 on the year and 2-1 in Midwestern League play, keeping pace in a tight league race.
The Millers, in the midst of their best season in several years, dropped to 3-1 and 2-1 in the MWL.
"It was a fun game — I think it was the funnest one so far this season," Thurston sophomore receiver Rocco Folino said. "They got us on the first, but we came back in the end and scored a whole bunch of points."
Thurston running back Quintin Fisher ran for 108 yards on eight carries. Quarterback Emmit Distefano went 9-for-15 passing for 103 yards and a touchdown. Bentlee Davenport caught three passes for 40 yards and two touchdowns, and Quinn Piquette also tallied 40 receiving yards.
For Springfield, senior quarterback Brayden Wickersheim threw for 233 yards and two touchdowns on 19-of-28 passing. He connected with Jackson Rich for 86 yards and a touchdown on four catches.
Springfield opened the scoring with an electric trick play that resulted in running back Josiah Stroud launching a 35-yard touchdown pass to Dakotah Short. Thurston answered with a few explosive running plays on the ensuing drive, and Distefano punched in a touchdown on a 4-yard rush up the middle to get the Colts on the board.
Then, Piquette, Thurston's all-league junior defensive back, turned the game on its head.
On the first play of a Springfield series, Piquette grabbed an interception at midfield, weaved his way through traffic, and took the ball to the end zone to give the Colts an early 14-7 lead.
"I was good on (Wickersheim) — just jumped inside and saw it. He just hucked it," Piquette said. "Just praying that it would go somewhere. First pick; really excited about that. Got to take it to the house."
Piquette was one of many Thurston players who generated havoc plays to shift the momentum. Later in the game, the Colts' fast-rising star sophomore, Rocco Folino, housed a pick-six of his own to pad his team's lead.
As a freshman last season, Folino was Thurston's junior varsity MVP. This fall, he has kicked up to the varsity level and made an immediate impact. In the win over the Millers, he delivered multiple big moments.
"He just works hard; he's a really athletic kid," Starck said. "He's a grinder. He's a riser, man. He's just getting better all the time."
As the Colts extended their lead, first-year offensive coordinator Blake Sentman opened up the playbook. Thurston's third touchdown of the night came on fourth down in Springfield territory. The Colts lined up to punt but unveiled a trick play that ended with Brody Baker lobbing a 22-yard touchdown pass to Ridge Lindsey.
Later, Davenport, an all-league receiver and defensive back, launched a 35-yard completion to all-state wideout Bodie Bonar.
"It's awesome; he is a great guy. He just believes in us," Piquette said of Sentman's impact on the program in his first year with the Colts. "We brought him in here, and he's making the most of it, giving us a strong look. It's just huge."
On its final drive, Thurston got backup quarterback Dean Knowles into the game for some meaningful reps. The junior marched the Colts' offense down the field and threw his first career touchdown pass — a 5-yard strike to Ethan Towns.
"I'm not trying to dog him or brag about myself. But man, he would start anywhere else in our league. He's a great quarterback. He's a great kid," Distefano said of Knowles. "He knows the offense like the back of his hand. He and I are really great friends. ... It means a lot to see him get that touchdown. I wanted him to get three more."
It's been a charmed couple of days for Distefano. At halftime of the win over the Millers, he was crowned Thurston's senior homecoming king.
Earlier this week, the Colts' signal-caller announced that he has committed to play at George Fox University.
"It's a Christian school; I've been working on my faith a lot these last few years," Distefano said of his decision to commit. "I've been following God a lot. (George Fox) is all about religion first, then football. We play the sport to worship God, and the talents that we have are because of him. The coaches are great; they actually want me. They only recruit two quarterbacks a year. ... It's not too far from home. I can still come up here and play golf wth my dad on the weekends. It's really great."

item.content:encoded:
Nærum Kulturhus introducerer et nyt initiativ, der kombinerer motion, naturoplevelser og fællesskab på tværs af alder og baggrund. Konceptet 'Ud at gå med Nærum Kulturhus' inviterer lokale borgere til at deltage i seks fælles gåture fra vinteren til det tidlige forår.
Gåturene finder sted i de naturskønne områder omkring Nærum. Kulturhusmedlem Liselotte Vejborg vil guide deltagerne gennem forskellige ruter i lokalområdet.

item.title: Celtic managerial twist as Robbie Keane is reportedly no longer under consideration
item.description: Robbie Keane is reportedly no longer being considered for the Celtic managerial position, despite recent speculation.
item.content:encoded:
Robbie Keane is reportedly now 'off the list' at Celtic amid renewed speculation over Martin O'Neill's future.
The former Hoops striker held highly-publicised talks with Celtic over the managerial vacancy during the summer before O'Neill ultimately remained in charge at Parkhead.
Keane was then named as a contender to replace Paul Heckingbottom at Preston last week, although the Championship club are now reportedly pushing to appoint former Motherwell boss Graham Alexander instead.
With O'Neill coming under increasing pressure following Celtic's recent run of results, Keane's name has inevitably resurfaced as a potential option should the club make a managerial change.
However, journalist Alan Nixon has suggested the Irishman is no longer under consideration at Parkhead.
Asked on X whether Keane had turned Celtic down, Nixon said: "I wouldn't put it like that, but it does seem he's off the list now. Maybe he thinks something better is coming."
Nixon also claimed there had been a 'snag' during Keane's discussions with Celtic in the summer.
He continued: "It was met with some protest, and O'Neill deciding to stay got them out of a hole at the time."
Keane's previous spell in charge of Maccabi Tel Aviv proved controversial among sections of the Celtic support when he was linked with the job.
The 46-year-old later took charge of Ferencvaros but departed at the end of last season after missing out on the Hungarian title to ETO FC Gyori, bringing the Budapest club's run of seven successive league championships to an end.
Keane retains strong connections to Celtic following his spell as a player and also has a long-standing relationship with the club's principal shareholder Dermot Desmond.
O'Neill, meanwhile, has not spoken publicly since last weekend's derby defeat to Rangers, after which he admitted he would take time to consider his own position.
Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson subsequently publicly backed the manager during the week, but uncertainty continues to surround what comes next at Parkhead.

That unfortunately will not last, as more scattered showers will redevelop this evening into the early overnight, especially south of Highway 30. An isolated thunderstorm is possible in the northwest corner of the state as well.

Severe weather is not expected, but heavy rainfall is a possibility. With the saturated conditions across the area, we will have to monitor the potential for flash flooding and river flooding.
The heavy rain should move out by Wednesday morning, but showers may linger for part of the day. The highest rain chance will be across southern Iowa. These showers could linger into Wednesday night and Thursday for some areas.

item.title: NFL picks: Who the experts predict to win in the Broncos-Rams game
item.description: Experts predict varied outcomes for the Week 3 NFL game between the Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Rams.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos (1-1) and Los Angeles Rams (1-1) have had similar starts to the 2026 season.
Each team was seen as a favorite to reach Super LXI, but each team suffered humbling, one-sided losses to divisional rivals in Week 1. However, each team bounced back in Week 2 with a big victory. Now they meet in a Week 3 prime-time showdown on Sunday Night Football in what many still see as a potential early-season Super Bowl preview.
How do the experts see this one going?
Broncos vs. Rams Week 3 expert picks
John Breech, CBS Sports: Broncos 23, Rams 21
"They should give the winner of this game a mini Lombardi Trophy since this is the Super Bowl we almost got last season", Breech wrote for CBS. "We came one injury and 6 yards away from getting this game, and honestly, based on how boring Super Bowl LX ended up being, I think I would have preferred this. On paper, I think these two teams are pretty evenly matched, but I think Rams will have two things working against them: They have to play on the road and they have to fly halfway across the country on a short week after playing Monday night.
The NFL scheduling department is clearly trying to break the Rams. After flying 15,842 miles round trip to Melbourne in Week 1, they're now adding 1,724 round-trip miles on this flight to Denver. By the end of Week 3, the Rams will have traveled more miles than 13 different teams will travel ALL SEASON.
That's a lot of jet lag, and as we know, the Rams don't deal well with jet lag. I'll take the Broncos in a thriller."
Gennaro Filice, NFL.com: Rams 23, Broncos 19
"The Super Bowl LX matchup that wasn't!", wrote Filice for NFL.com. "Eight months ago, the Rams and Broncos suffered narrow defeats on Championship Sunday, leaving both painfully short of the Lombardi Trophy game. Then they opened this season by hitting the road and humiliating themselves on national television. Both returned to form at home in Week 2, though, setting up a compelling clash worthy of the Sunday night stage. Showcasing a pair of Super Bowl-winning head coaches and two of the league's most well-rounded rosters, this game doesn't lack for star power. And yet, I see its outcome hinging on the Rams' meat and potatoes, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. With eerily similar frames, games and jersey numbers (23 and 24), L.A.'s two backs are difficult to tell apart. And so is their robust ground production through two games.
I see Los Angeles' blue-collar backfield playing a leading role in this prime-time tilt. Denver cleaned up its tackling last week after an embarrassing display against Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III, but I still think this front's susceptible to the run. Free-agent departure John Franklin-Myers got $63 million for a reason."
Bill Bender, The Sporting News: Broncos 23, Rams 21
"It's a tough road game for the Rams. Denver's pass defense ranks seventh in the NFL, and Bo Nix is 15-3 at home as a starter. With Los Angeles coming off a short week, this is a tough assignment for Matthew Stafford with injuries to Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett, who is out. The Broncos are 5-1-1 ATS as an underdog since last season", wrote Bender for The Sporting News.
Jeremy Cluff, Arizona Republic: Rams 27, Broncos 24
"NBC gets a good one for Sunday Night Football in NFL Week 3 with Matthew Stafford vs. Bo Nix and two elite defenses", Cluff wrote for Arizona Republic. "This one might come down to which defense steps up late. It will be the road team."

item.title: 14 Trader Joe's 2026 Fall Sweet Treats That Aren't Pumpkin Or Pumpkin Spice Flavored
item.description: This article lists 14 non-pumpkin fall sweet treats available at Trader Joe's, including apple, maple, and chocolate-flavored items.
item.content:encoded:
Fall is always overrun by pumpkin spiced lattes and the introduction of too many pumpkin-flavored foods — some of which probably never should have hit the market. If you're not a pumpkin person, Trader Joe's has you covered. The fan-favorite grocery store launches so many fall treats this time of year, and while many are pumpkin-flavored, we found 14 delicious fall treats flavored with anything but pumpkin.
Apple is an iconic fall flavor right up there with pumpkin, so a few of those are on the list, but we also found some tasty maple-forward treats that we had to include. Fall fruit flavors, such as plum, make up at least one or two of these choices, and there's a great balance between cookies, chocolates, and even donuts. If you're a TJ's fan who craves the warmth of fall flavors but longs to escape the world of pumpkin everything, treat yourself to one — or all — of these sweets.
Apple Crisp Milk Chocolate Caramels
This treat has all the flavors of an apple crisp, but it's wrapped in a milk chocolate caramel treat rather than in the typical baked dessert. These are finished with a streusel-like crunchy bottom, too.
The Apple Crisp Milk Chocolate Caramels are $5.99 per package.
Plum Torte
The Trader Joe's Plum Torte is a great dish to buy if you're hosting a fall brunch, or want a fruit-forward dessert to serve guests. The torte is frozen, so just bake it until it's warm. Serve it up with a scoop of vanilla ice cream if you wish.
Grab the Plum Torte at Trader Joe's for $7.99.
Cinnamon Powdered Sugar Mini Donuts
These packaged donuts are perfect for grabbing a sweet fall treat on the go, for dipping into coffee, or even for enjoying as a post-breakfast dessert. They're coated in the perfect blend of cinnamon and sugar (always a winning donut combo) and offer a crumbly, yet dense, texture.
The Cinnamon Powdered Sugar Mini Donuts are at Trader Joe's for $4.49.
Autumn Leaf Sugar Cookies
Nothing says autumn like falling leaves. While the flavor of these sugar cookies is pretty standard, it's the shape that gives them the fall twist. These are great for adding to a dessert tray, or even as a sweet element of a charcuterie board.
The Autumn Leaf Sugar Cookies are available for $3.99 per box.
Apple Cider Donuts
What is fall without indulging in at least one or two apple cider donuts? These are often found at orchards and farmers markets, but Trader Joe's makes them easily accessible to anyone. If you toast these, or microwave them for just a few seconds to warm them up, you won't regret it.
The Apple Cider Donuts cost $4.99 per box.
Wicked Good Mini Chocolate Bars
These chocolate candies are perfect to hand out on Halloween. They have fall-themed wrapping foil and come in four flavors: nougat, nougat and caramel, peanut and caramel, and caramel and wafer. The trick or treaters should appreciate them, but don't forget to set a few aside for yourself.
Grab a bag of the Wicked Good Mini Chocolate Bars for $4.99.
Halloween Joe-Joe's Cookies
These cookies have pumpkin patterns, but we promise they aren't pumpkin flavored. The Halloween Joe-Joe's are similar to Oreos, but the filling is dyed orange, and each chocolate wafer has the face of a Jack-o'-lantern.
A bag of Halloween Joe-Joe's Cookies is available for $4.49.
Rustic Apple Tarte
The Rustic Apple Tarte is a frozen treat that makes your whole home smell like fall once it goes in the oven. It's made with both sweet and tart apples, combined with cinnamon, sugar, and cream cheese, all at the center of a flaky pastry. This is the perfect addition to a brunch, or a wonderful fall dessert when paired with ice cream.
The Rustic Apple Tarte costs $5.99.
All Butter Apple Shortbread Cookies
A melt-in-your-mouth shortbread cookie is hard to resist. When it's apple flavored, it becomes the perfect fall snack. These are great for eating on their own, or for turning into mini fall ice cream sandwiches with a scoop of vanilla between each cookie.
The All Butter Apple Shortbread Cookies are available for $3.79 per package.
Salted Maple Ice Cream
Ice cream can (and should) be enjoyed any time of year, and this salted maple ice cream — made with real maple syrup — is the perfect way to indulge in the cooler fall months.A little sea salt balances out the sweetness. Enjoy this ice cream on its own, add a scoop to some hot chocolate, or smush it between those apple shortbread cookies.
The Salted Maple Ice Cream is available for $3.79 per pint.
Mini Maple Flavored Marshmallows
You might pop a handful of these mini marshmallows in your mouth for a quick snack, but they're better when baked into a dessert. The maple flavor makes these a great fall ingredient for mind-blowing Rice Krispie treats, but these also work with homemade brownies or even cupcakes.
The Mini Maple Flavored Marshmallows cost $2.99 per bag.
Maple Butterscotch Blondie Baking Mix
Maple blondies sound amazing, and we could see them becoming a yearly fall staple at TJ's. It's a boxed mix, but these aren't hard to put together (all you need to add is an egg and some melted butter), and you can tell your friends they're sort of homemade. The maple and butterscotch flavors really go to work here.
The Maple Butterscotch Blondie Baking Mix costs $4.99.
Harvest Chocolate Collection
The Harvest Chocolate Collection is the perfect host or hostess gift for the fall season. The chocolates are just as pretty as they are tasty, and there are nine to a box.It includes milk, dark, and white chocolates in fun fall shapes, with an assortment of fillings and flavors including caramel and hazelnut.
The Harvest Chocolate Collection is available for $5.49.
Pumpkins Sugar Cookie Dough
This treat is great when you want the house to smell like sugar cookies, but don't want to make them from scratch. There are pumpkins, yes, but no pumpkin flavor. The sugar cookies are a break-and-bake style that come premeasured and ready for the oven.
Grab a package of Pumpkins Sugar Cookie Dough for $3.99.

item.title: How to do a basic squat
item.description: This article provides a step-by-step guide on how to perform a basic bodyweight squat for beginners.
item.content:encoded:
How to do a basic squat
For beginners who want stronger legs and steadier balance using only body weight.
Every squat works when your heels stay planted and your chest stays tall so the work stays in your legs instead of your lower back.
Clear a six-foot by six-foot floor space and wear shoes with flat soles.
1: STAND with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out fifteen degrees, and arms hanging relaxed.
You'll need only open floor and clothes you can bend in. You know the stance is set when you can lift your toes slightly yet both heels stay glued to the ground.
2: BRACE your midsection by inhaling deeply and tightening as if preparing for a light poke to the stomach.
Ribs draw down and the lower back stays neutral. You feel it is ready when the tightness holds even while you take short breaths.
3: LOWER your hips back and down as though sitting into a chair just behind you.
Knees track in line with the toes and the chest stays lifted. You know the depth is right when thighs reach roughly parallel to the floor and you feel the hips stretch.
4: HOLD the bottom for a slow one-count while keeping heels down and knees pushed gently out.
Balance stays even across both feet. You know the pause worked when you could still wiggle your toes without rocking forward.
5: DRIVE through your heels to rise, exhaling and squeezing the glutes as you return to stand.
Hips and knees finish locked. You know the rep is complete when you stand tall with the same braced midsection you started with.
The most common mistake
Knees collapsing inward shifts stress to the joints. Push the knees outward so they stay stacked over the toes for the whole movement.
Pro tip
Do three sets of eight smooth reps and rest sixty seconds between sets before adding any load.
Say it every time
heels down chest tall knees out drive up

item.title: How to do a push-up
item.description: This article provides a step-by-step guide on how to perform a push-up, including common mistakes and a modification for beginners.
item.content:encoded:
For beginners who want chest, arm and core strength with a move that needs only floor space.
Keep your body stiff in one straight line from the crown of your head to your heels. That single rigid line is what turns the bend of your elbows into work for your chest and arms instead of strain on your lower back.
Clear six feet of open floor. Wear a shirt and shorts that let your shoulders move and keep bare feet or flat shoes.
**1: PLACE** your palms flat on the floor directly under your shoulders with fingers spread and pointing forward.
You'll need the six-foot floor space already cleared; a thin mat is optional under the hands. You know the placement is right when each arm hangs straight down and you can see your hands framing your face as you look between them.
**2: EXTEND** both legs straight behind you until only your palms and the balls of your feet touch the floor.
Walk the feet back one at a time while the hands stay fixed. You know the high plank is ready when your body forms one long line and your feet sit roughly hip-width apart. If you wobble, move the feet one inch wider.
**3: BRACE** your midsection by pulling the belly button toward the spine and squeezing the glutes.
Keep the head in line with the spine so you gaze at the floor a foot ahead. You feel the brace lock when the hips stay level with the shoulders and the whole torso goes firm. Hold that tension without holding your breath.
**4: LOWER** your chest by bending the elbows until they reach a ninety-degree angle.
Elbows stay close to the body at roughly forty-five degrees from your sides. You know the depth is correct when your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your chest hovers about one inch above it. Move for a slow two-count down.
**5: DRIVE** through your palms to straighten the arms and return to the high plank.
Exhale on the way up. You know the rep is finished when the elbows straighten softly and the head-to-heel line is straight again at the top. Do not let the shoulders shrug toward the ears.
**6: REPEAT** the lower-and-drive sequence for eight to twelve controlled reps.
Reset the brace before every descent. You know the set is complete when the final rep still shows a straight body line and you can hold the top plank for two full seconds. Rest sixty seconds if you plan another set.
### The most common mistake
Hips sag or pike when the core loosens mid-rep. Fix it by re-bracing the belly and glutes before each lower and checking the side-view line stays flat.
### Pro tip
If full toe push-ups feel too hard, drop both knees to the floor and keep the same hand placement, brace, lower and drive until you can add the toes.
### Say it every time
**Place brace lower drive**

Final: Notre Dame 49, Purdue 10
05:13 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Purdue managed to get a garbage-time touchdown, with just a few seconds left in the game. It really doesn't matter much, as the game was already decided quite a long time ago. Notre Dame improves to 4-0, while Purdue falls to 1-3 on the season. The Irish stay on the road next weekend, as they will travel to take on North Carolina.
Matt Jeffery catches first career touchdown (Q4, 4:05)
05:02 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
The second drive for the second-team was much better than the first, as Walton ripped off a 44-yard run to put the Irish at the Purdue 5 yard line. The coaching staff tried to get Walton the score, but after two unsuccessful tries, Grubbs found Jeffery in the end zone for a score. More Walton please.
Notre Dame's offensive backups are in, but not productive (Q4, 7:38)
04:51 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Carr's day is done and it was Noah Grubb's turn to run the offense. It was a quick showing for the backup, as a 4-yard Jonaz Walton run followed by back-to-back incompletions saw the drive end. I'd like to see more of the freshman back, maybe he can be a spark later in the season. The second-team defense isn't having any issues, as it got off the field quickly after a 4-play, 9-yard drive ended by a Rodney Dunham sack.
Purdue goes three-and-out, punts ball back (Q4, 11:19)
04:43 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
The Boilers have made a change at quarterback with Evans Chuba now in. The result was much of the same, as the Irish defense once again rose up to the challenge. It was the best effort of the day, resulting in a three-and-out.
Carr gets back into groove, finds Cooper Flanagan for score (Q4, 13:30)
04:33 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
The law firm of Flanagan and Flanigan showed up today, as Cooper's second reception was a 2-yard touchdown. They've combined for three catches for 38-yards, and while those aren't huge numbers, it's a great development within Notre Dame's offense.
Notre Dame loses third quarter to Purdue (end of third)
04:27 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
That was not the best quarter for the Irish, as Carr first pick of the year saw the offense really struggle for the first time all day. The Boilers won the third, 3-0, and while they really didn't help themselves much, it's something to build on. The opposite for Notre Dame, they now have areas to work on after a not great quarter.
Purdue gets points, settles for field goal (Q3, 4:10)
04:18 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
It didn't look like the Boilers could put anything together on offense, but they took advantage of another short field with some solid early plays. The shutout won't happen, as Purdue made a 47-yard field goal to finally get on the scoreboard.
Notre Dame offense sputters, punts ball back to Purdue (Q3, 7:45)
04:11 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
It was interesting to see the response by the Irish offense to Carr's first pick of the year, and they went very conservative. Three straight runs didn't net 10-yards, and saw Notre Dame punt the ball back to the Boilers. Not a big fan of that drive, I would have like to see Carr throw it to get his confidence back.
Notre Dame makes its first mistake, Carr throws interception (Q3, 9:48)
04:04 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
This wasn't the start that the Irish were looking for, as they got the ball first after the half, with the intention of extending the lead. Instead, Carr threw an ill advised pass over the middle of the field that was picked off. Purdue had great field position, but again, struggled to move the ball as Notre Dame's defense stepped up in the red zone, holding the Boilers without points after a failed 4th down conversion.
Notre Dame 35, Purdue 0 - 3 halftime observations
03:36 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
1 - A complete performance by the Irish, as the offense looked great but passing and running. Defensively, just 90-yards allowed, and they've outscored the Boilers.
2 - CJ Carr is on fire, and it's not just about his state. He's 9-of-15 for 186-yards and 2 touchdowns, while adding 10-yards and another score on the ground. Carr's command of the offense is elite, often checking to the right play.
3 - The sack party is happening, with four Irish players registering at least part of one during the first half. Hard to say that this group isn't one of the best in the nation, as they've dismantled the Purdue offense.
Carr finds James, Notre Dame's lead extends (Q2, 0:29)
03:31 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
A perfect two-minute drive, as the Irish went 49-yards in 6-plays with just over a minute in game time used. This is the exact scenario that coaches want to see, and Notre Dame offense executed it perfectly. Great drive with the ability to add another score after the half and really put this game out of reach.
Purdue eating up clock again, but not going anywhere (Q2, 2 minute warning)
03:23 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Purdue once again is holding onto the ball, but not really moving down the field. They took just over 2 minutes to run just five plays, it's clear now they're trying to play keep away. It might keep the score somewhat close, but it's not a recipe for a win.
Bryce Young forces fumble, Drayk Bowen with the scoop and score (Q2, 4:15)
03:17 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
As previously said, this could get ugly quick, and it's starting to look like it. The Irish defense once again put points on the board, and Young, who is having a fantastic game, got a sack, forced the fumble and Bowen picked it up and ran 15-yards untouched for the score. Notre Dame is officially rolling, and we could see the backups in early during the third quarter.
Notre Dame's 85-yard drive capped by Carr rushing touchdown
03:10 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Purdue has been grinding out drives all game, or at least trying to, and the Irish had one of their own. Notre Dame went 13-plays for 85-yards capped off with a designed Carr rushing touchdown. The biggest play of the drive was a 27-yard pass from Carr to tight end Cooper Flanagan, which was nice to see after that group was shut out last week. The Irish are starting to roll, and this one could get ugly quick.
Aneyas Willams gets Notre Dame's first 20-yard rush of 2026, scores (Q2, 11:46)
02:55 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
It didn't take long for the Irish to find the end zone in the second quarter, as Williams finally breaks the 20-yard mark in a single-rush ending the 2026 season drought. It went for 22-yards, and his score is the third of the season. The run game looks like it's figuring it out, which is the key to unlocking this Notre Dame offense. Mukam again has a big play, getting a sack, forcing a 3rd-and-13, and Joey O'Brien makes his presence known with his first-career sack. The Irish are starting to roll.
Notre Dame driving as first quarter ends
02:46 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
The emergence of Gilbert has been huge, and once again it paid off, as Carr found him for a 56-yard strike flipping the field. After 170-yards last week, he's already up to 83 with a score today. Huge development for the Irish offense.
Armel Mukam and Francis Brewu come up big, Notre Dame forces punt (Q1, 1:18)
02:42 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Purdue badly wanted to answer the Irish's touchdown, but couldn't get anything moving in the right direction. A 3rd-and-short saw Mukam and Brewu combine for a tackle-for-loss stopping the drive. Great job by the Notre Dame defense to quickly get the ball back to the offense. Another touchdown and the rout could be getting started.
Leonard Moore allows a catch, Purdue tries to get tricky and fails (Q1, 4:09)
02:33 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Teams haven't tested Moore often this fall, and the Boilers have twice, and finally a successful on. It didn't go far, just 4-yards, which eventually set up a 4th-and-four, which Purdue tried to run a fake. They were just inches short of making it, giving the Irish great field position. Carr finds Jordan Faison for the second time this game, another solid chunk going for 17-yards. The offense is trying to give James as many touches as possible, and he had a nice 7-yard run. Carr would find Gilbert for a 27-yard touchdown strike to start the scoring. Great drive, with some positive rushing plays.
Notre Dame 7, Purdue 0
Purdue slowly making its way down the field vs. Notre Dame (Q1, 8:19)
02:23 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
A Boiler injury has sent the game to a timeout, as they are methodically moving the ball down the field. So far 7-play spanning 29-yards taking up almost 3:00 minutes of time. This dink and dunk isn't going to work against the Irish defense.
Purdue wins toss, gives it right back to Notre Dame (Q1, 11:28)
02:14 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
Interestingly, the Boilermakers won the toss and opted to take the ball first. Typically teams at home will want the ball to start the second half, as it was a disaster. Irish defensive lineman Bryce Young sacked Ryan Browne on the first play from scrimmage, as two pass plays didn't result in much yardage. Notre Dame started its drive with a pass plays didn't result, which isn't surprising considering the run game issues. Nolan James Jr. got the first carry, as he earned it after last week's performance. The drive stalled after two incomplete passes with the run between. Not the best start for the Irish.
Notre Dame at Purdue's kickoff is soon
01:57 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
If you are looking for the game on broadcast television, I've got bad news for you, it's only available via streaming on Peacock. The game should be an interesting one, where the Irish could be working on areas that need improvement. Kickoff coming up in a few minutes.
Notre Dame football: Three things I'm interested to see vs. Purdue
01:29 PM ET, September 26 2026, Michael Chen
1 - Notre Dame's run game: Will we see some improvement now that Nolan James Jr. is getting more reps? Can Aneyas Williams finally get comfortable? It will be interesting to see how this group performs.
2 - Joey O'Brien's first start: The former 5-star earned playing time, but it was expected more as a super-sub instead of a starter. A pair of injuries to Brauntae Johnson and Luke Talich have opened the opportunity. This is a perfect game for him to really get his feet wet.
